posts.igCaptionLong:
New build on the bench, and this one comes with some serious history.

These boards spent over a hundred years as part of a barn. The old hinges and nails came out of them before anything else happened. The wood is old-growth pine, so the trees were growing long before anyone thought of building that barn. You can see it in the end grain: tight rings, slow growth, the kind of wood you can't just order.

Every Sixto gets a name from the wood's previous life. This one is Horreum: Latin for barn.

The body is glued up and will become a semi-hollow, the neck has its truss rod, and the fretboard is next. And yes, sighting down a neck with one eye closed is a perfectly legitimate measuring technique.

Follow along to see a barn turn into a guitar.
